Ethanethiol, CH$_3$CH$_2$SH, is a foul-smelling gas that is added to natural gas to enable humans to detect gas leaks, which would otherwise not be noticed.
The minimum concentration of ethanethiol that a person can detect is $1.8 \times 10^{-7}$ mg per cm$^3$ of air.
A gas leak happens in an empty room that has dimensions $20 \text{ m} \times 20 \text{ m} \times 3 \text{ m}$. Assume that the ethanethiol is spread evenly throughout the room.
If a person detected the gas leak, what is the minimum number of molecules of ethanethiol in the room to 1 significant figure?
(A$_r$ values: H = 1; C = 12; S = 32. Avogadro's number = $6 \times 10^{23}$)
